# Design: Localized structural keywords for specs and deltas

## Context

Observed in the code today, every structural keyword is an English literal at
its point of use:

- `codev-core/src/parser/shared.rs` — `requirement_header` strips
  `"### Requirement:"`, `scenario_header` strips `"#### Scenario:"`,
  `wrong_level_scenario` strips `"### Scenario:"`, and `delta_section_kind`
  upper-cases the title, strips the suffix `REQUIREMENTS`, then matches
  `ADDED` / `MODIFIED` / `REMOVED` / `RENAMED`.
- `parser/spec.rs` finds the sections with
  `title.eq_ignore_ascii_case("Purpose")` and `"Requirements"`;
  `parser/delta.rs` does the same for `Purpose`, reads `**Reason**` /
  `**Migration**` through `find_labelled_line(body, "Reason")`, the rename
  pair through `strip_prefix("FROM:")` / `"TO:"`, the heading form of a rename
  through `strip_prefix("### Requirement:")`, and classifies unexpected
  `### ` headings with `starts_with("Requirement:")` / `"Scenario:"`. Its
  hint says "the keyword stays in English whatever the artifact language".
- `validate/rules.rs::check_requirement_shall` tests
  `description.contains("SHALL") || contains("MUST")`.
- `merge/render.rs` writes `"### Requirement: "` and `"#### Scenario: "`;
  `merge/mod.rs` rewrites a renamed heading with
  `format!("### Requirement: {}", rename.to)` over the whole heading line, and
  `build_new_spec` writes `"# <Title> Specification"`, `"## Purpose"` and
  `"## Requirements"`.

The callers in `codev-engine` (`sync.rs`, `validate/mod.rs`, `changelog.rs`)
only call `parse_spec` / `parse_delta` and the merge; the CLI never matches a
keyword. `parse_spec(source)` and `parse_delta(source)` take no configuration.

Constraints: decision 0001 (functional core, imperative shell) — the catalog
and all matching live in `codev-core` with no I/O; decision 0002 (the crate
graph is the dependency rule) — nothing new crosses a crate boundary. The
JSON contract (`codev-cli::contract::v1`) must not change shape.

## Goals / Non-Goals

**Goals**

- One place, `codev-core`, that knows every structural keyword of every
  supported language; adding a language is adding one catalog entry plus its
  tests.
- English files parse, validate and merge to the same bytes as today.

**Non-Goals**

- Proposal, design, tasks and review-record headings (`## Why`,
  `## Domains`, `## Release note`, read by `parser/section.rs`): unchanged.
- Skills and templates: they keep writing English keywords.
- Translating prose or normative keywords during a merge.
- A user-defined catalog in `_codev/config.yaml`: the catalog is built in.

## Decisions

### Decision: A static catalog in `codev-core`, one entry per language

A new module `codev-core/src/keywords.rs` holds:

```rust
pub struct Keywords {
    pub lang: &'static str,           // "en", "fr"
    pub purpose: &'static str,        // "Purpose" / "Objectif"
    pub requirements: &'static str,   // "Requirements" / "Exigences"
    pub requirement: &'static str,    // "Requirement" / "Exigence"
    pub scenario: &'static str,       // "Scenario" / "Scénario"
    pub delta: DeltaHeadings,         // full titles per DeltaKind
    pub reason: &'static str,
    pub migration: &'static str,
    pub from: &'static str,
    pub to: &'static str,
    pub normative: &'static [&'static str],
    pub title: fn(&str) -> String,    // "<T> Specification" / "Spécification <T>"
}
pub static CATALOG: &[Keywords] = &[EN, FR];
```

Keywords are stored without their `#` level and without the colon: the
level belongs to the grammar (the parser keeps owning "exactly four hashes"),
and the colon tolerance is one rule for all languages. Delta headings are
stored as whole titles (`ADDED Requirements`, `Exigences AJOUTÉES`) because
word order differs between languages; the current "strip the suffix
`REQUIREMENTS`" trick cannot express French.

Plain `&'static` data, no YAML file: a catalog read at run time would need
I/O in the core (decision 0001) or a new embedded-asset path, for a list
that changes only with a codev release.

**Alternatives considered**: a `HashMap<Keyword, &str>` per language —
rejected, a missing keyword becomes a runtime gap instead of a compile
error; a YAML catalog embedded like the schemas — rejected, it adds parsing
and an error path for data that no user edits.

### Decision: Matching helpers in the catalog module; the parser asks them

`keywords.rs` exposes the only functions that compare text with a keyword:

- `match_heading_title(title) -> Option<(SectionKeyword, &'static Keywords)>`
  for `## ` titles (Purpose, Requirements, the four delta kinds);
- `strip_labelled(line, Label) -> Option<(&str rest, &'static Keywords)>`
  for `Requirement`, `Scenario`, `Reason`, `Migration`, `FROM`, `TO`: it
  accepts the keyword, then optional spaces (`' '`, U+00A0, U+202F), then
  `:`; the rest is returned trimmed;
- `has_normative(text) -> bool`, an exact-uppercase substring test over the
  normative keywords of every language — the same test as today's for
  English, so English results are unchanged.

Comparison folds case with `str::to_lowercase` (Unicode, needed for `É`)
and folds accents through a small table limited to the letters the catalog
uses (`é è ê à ç` and their capitals). No new dependency: the catalog's
letters are known, and a general Unicode normalisation crate would be
heavier than the problem.

The parser's existing functions keep their names and roles —
`requirement_header`, `scenario_header`, `wrong_level_scenario`,
`delta_section_kind`, `find_labelled_line`, `parse_renames`, the Purpose and
Requirements lookups — and call these helpers instead of their literals.
Every catalogued language is tried, in catalog order (English first); the
first match wins. Two spellings coincide across languages — `Migration`, and
`Scenario` once accents are folded — and both mean the same thing in both
languages; the language reported by a match is only used for the
`## Requirements` and `## Purpose` headings, whose spellings never coincide.
The order therefore does not change a result.

The hint of `delta_unexpected_heading` and the message of
`requirement_no_shall` are built from `CATALOG`, so they name every accepted
form (`### Requirement:` / `### Exigence :`; `SHALL`, `MUST`, `DOIT`,
`DOIVENT`). Codes and severities do not change.

**Alternatives considered**: passing the configured `language:` into
`parse_spec` / `parse_delta` and recognizing only English plus that
language — rejected, see the next decision; one regular expression per
keyword built from the catalog with `regex-automata` (already a dependency)
— rejected, the matches are prefix tests on one line and plain string code
keeps the byte positions obvious, which `Span` depends on.

### Decision: Recognition ignores `language:`

`parse_spec` and `parse_delta` keep their signatures and recognize every
catalogued language. Tying recognition to the configured language would
make a file's validity depend on a configuration key: a project that
changed `language:` after writing its specs would see them break, and an
inherited or shared spec would be valid in one project and not another. The
only cost is that `## Objectif` in an English-only project is read as a
Purpose heading rather than a free section, which the risks below cover.

**Alternatives considered**: English plus the configured language —
rejected for the reasons above, and it would add a configuration read to
`sync.rs`, `validate/mod.rs` and `changelog.rs` for no user benefit.

### Decision: The AST records the language of the headings the merge needs

`Spec` gains `lang: &'static str`, the language of its `## Requirements`
heading (`"en"` when absent). `PurposeBlock` gains `lang`, the language of
the `## Purpose` heading it was read from, used only for a new main spec.
`Requirement` gains `header_name_range: Range<usize>`, the byte range of the
name inside its heading line.

The merge uses them:

- `render::requirement` and `scenario_str` take a `&Keywords` and write
  `### {requirement}{sep}: ` / `#### {scenario}{sep}: `, where `sep` is `""`
  for English and `" "` for French — a field of the catalog entry, so the
  rendering of English is byte-identical to today;
- `ADDED` and `MODIFIED` render with the keywords of `spec.lang`;
- `RENAMED` edits only `header_name_range`, replacing today's rewrite of the
  whole heading line. For an English heading written `### Requirement: X`
  the result is the same bytes as today;
- `build_new_spec` renders the title, Purpose and Requirements headings and
  the requirements with the keywords of `delta.purpose.lang`.

Descriptions and scenario bodies are copied as they are today: the merge
does not translate prose.

**Alternatives considered**: detecting the language of a main spec by
counting the keywords of each language — rejected, it is harder to explain
and to test than "the language of the `## Requirements` heading", and a tie
needs another rule; keeping the delta's own keywords when merging —
rejected, it is the behavior the request asks to avoid.

## Risks / Trade-offs

- [An existing English spec of some project holds a free-form section titled
  `## Objectif` or `## Exigences`, which is now read as a Purpose or
  Requirements heading] → the lookups keep taking the first matching
  heading, as they do today, so such a section placed after the English one
  changes nothing; a section placed before it would, which is unlikely in a
  file codev generated. The release note names the French headings, and a
  corpus test runs the parser over every main spec and archived delta of
  this repository and asserts the parsed result is unchanged.
- [Accent and space folding widens what is accepted; a typo such as
  `### Exigence :Mode` is accepted] → the tolerance is limited to the
  catalogued keywords and to spaces before the colon; the name after it is
  trimmed exactly as today.
- [`Span` byte ranges go wrong with multi-byte keywords (`É` is two bytes in
  UTF-8)] → the helpers return slices of the original line, never indices
  into a lowercased copy; unit tests assert the spans of a French requirement
  and scenario.
- [English output drifts by a byte] → golden tests of the existing merge
  suite stay unchanged and must pass untouched; any diff in them is a defect
  of this change.
- [The skills still tell agents that a translated keyword is a broken
  artifact] → the statement stays true for languages outside the catalog;
  rewording the skill and teaching it to write French keywords is left to a
  follow-up change, recorded as a non-goal.

## Migration Plan

No data or configuration migration: every existing file is read as before,
and no key is added. Rollback is reverting the change; French-keyword specs
written meanwhile would then fail validation again, as they do today.

# Proposal: Localized structural keywords for specs and deltas

## Why

A team that writes its specs in French must still type the structural
keywords in English (`### Requirement:`, `## ADDED Requirements`, `SHALL`…):
otherwise validation rejects the file, and sync and archive refuse the change.
These keywords are hard-coded across the parser, the validator and the merge,
so supporting another language today means touching every one of them. A
single per-language keyword catalog lets codev read French specs, and lets
the next language be added in one place.

## What Changes

- A keyword catalog per language, built into codev, holds every structural
  keyword of a main spec and a delta: `## Purpose`, `## Requirements`,
  `### Requirement:`, `#### Scenario:`, the four delta section headings,
  `**Reason**`, `**Migration**`, `FROM:` / `TO:`, the normative keywords
  `SHALL` / `MUST`, and the title of a new main spec. It ships with two
  languages: English (`en`) and French (`fr`, e.g. `### Exigence :`,
  `## Exigences AJOUTÉES`, `DOIT`).
- The parser recognizes the keywords of every language of the catalog, in any
  spec or delta, whatever the project's `language:`. English keeps working
  exactly as today.
- Validation accepts the normative keywords of every catalogued language for
  the `requirement_no_shall` rule, and its messages name the accepted forms
  instead of saying the keyword must be English.
- Sync and archive keep the language of the main spec they modify: the
  requirement and scenario headings they write or retitle use that spec's
  keywords, whatever language the delta is written in. A main spec created
  for a new capability takes the language of the delta's `## Purpose`
  heading.
- Nothing else changes: existing English specs and deltas parse, validate and
  merge to the same bytes as before.

Assumptions made without asking (evaluation run, no user to ask):

- **Recognition does not depend on `language:`.** Every catalogued language
  is recognized in every project. Tying recognition to `language:` would
  break a project whose specs predate a change of that key, and would make
  the same file valid or invalid depending on the configuration.
- **French keywords** are the ones listed in the `spec-keywords` spec. Accents
  are optional in the keywords (`Scenario :` and `Scénario :` both read), and
  the colon may be preceded by a space or a non-breaking space, as French
  typography uses.
- **Scope is the spec and delta format only.** The headings of the proposal,
  design and tasks (`## Why`, `## Domains`, `## Release note`…) and of the
  review record stay English-only. Scenario steps (`**GIVEN**`, `**WHEN**`,
  `**THEN**`) are not parsed by codev today, so they need no catalog entry.
- **The skills keep writing English keywords.** English stays valid
  everywhere; teaching `/codev-propose` and `/codev-update` to write the
  configured language's keywords is a separate change.
- **No mixed-language warning.** A file mixing English and French keywords is
  accepted; the language of a main spec, for the merge, is the language of
  its `## Requirements` heading.

## Capabilities

### New Capabilities

- `spec-keywords`

### Modified Capabilities

- `spec-parsing`
- `validation`
- `spec-merge`

### Removed Capabilities

## Impact

- `codev-core`: a new keyword catalog module (pure data); the parser
  (`parser/shared.rs`, `parser/spec.rs`, `parser/delta.rs`) matches through
  it; `validate/rules.rs` checks normative keywords through it;
  `merge/mod.rs` and `merge/render.rs` render headings in the target spec's
  language. The parsed AST gains the language of a spec and of a delta's
  Purpose.
- `codev-engine`: no new reading of the configuration; `sync.rs`,
  `validate/` and `changelog.rs` keep calling the same parser entry points.
- JSON contract (`codev-cli::contract::v1`): unchanged — codes, fields and
  shapes stay the same; only some message texts change.
- Documentation, in both `docs/en` and `docs/fr`:
  `guides/artifact-language.md` (the "what is translated" section and its
  warning) and `reference/file-formats.md` (the keyword table).

## Domains

- [ ] security
- [ ] personal-data
- [ ] user-interface
- [ ] performance
- [ ] operations
- [x] migration

## Release note

- Added: Specs and deltas can be written with French structural keywords
  (`## Objectif`, `### Exigence :`, `#### Scénario :`, `## Exigences
  AJOUTÉES`, `DOIT`…); `codev validate`, `codev sync` and `codev archive`
  recognize them alongside the English ones.
- Changed: `codev sync` and `codev archive` write requirement and scenario
  headings in the language of the main spec they modify, so a French spec
  stays French when an English delta is merged into it.

## Purpose

Define, per language, the structural keywords codev reads in main specs and
deltas, so that a team can write its specs entirely in its own language and
every command — validation, sync, archive — recognizes the same keywords.

## ADDED Requirements

### Requirement: A keyword catalog per language

codev SHALL carry a catalog that gives, for each supported language, the
form of every structural keyword of a main spec and a delta. The catalog
MUST hold English (`en`) and French (`fr`), with these forms:

| Keyword | `en` | `fr` |
|---|---|---|
| Purpose section | `## Purpose` | `## Objectif` |
| Requirements section | `## Requirements` | `## Exigences` |
| Requirement heading | `### Requirement: <name>` | `### Exigence : <name>` |
| Scenario heading | `#### Scenario: <name>` | `#### Scénario : <name>` |
| Added section | `## ADDED Requirements` | `## Exigences AJOUTÉES` |
| Modified section | `## MODIFIED Requirements` | `## Exigences MODIFIÉES` |
| Removed section | `## REMOVED Requirements` | `## Exigences SUPPRIMÉES` |
| Renamed section | `## RENAMED Requirements` | `## Exigences RENOMMÉES` |
| Removal reason | `**Reason**:` | `**Raison** :` |
| Removal migration | `**Migration**:` | `**Migration** :` |
| Rename pair | `FROM:` / `TO:` | `DE :` / `VERS :` |
| Normative keywords | `SHALL`, `MUST` | `DOIT`, `DOIVENT` |
| Title of a new main spec | `# <Title> Specification` | `# Spécification <Title>` |

Scenario steps (`**GIVEN**`, `**WHEN**`, `**THEN**`, `**AND**`) are free
text that codev does not parse; they are not part of the catalog, and any
language MAY be used for them.

#### Scenario: A main spec written with French keywords

- **GIVEN** a main spec holding `## Objectif`, a sentence, `## Exigences`,
  then a requirement headed `### Exigence : Mode sombre` whose description
  contains `DOIT` and which has a scenario headed `#### Scénario : Système
  en mode sombre`
- **WHEN** the user runs `codev validate --specs`
- **THEN** the spec is valid
- **AND** its requirement `Mode sombre` and its scenario
  `Système en mode sombre` are recognized

#### Scenario: An English spec is read as before

- **GIVEN** a main spec written with the English keywords only
- **WHEN** the user runs `codev validate --specs --json`
- **THEN** the report is identical to the one codev produced before the
  catalog existed

#### Scenario: A language outside the catalog is not recognized

- **GIVEN** a delta whose `## ADDED Requirements` section holds the heading
  `### Anforderung: Dunkelmodus`
- **WHEN** the user runs `codev validate <change>`
- **THEN** the heading is not recognized as a requirement and an error
  `delta_unexpected_heading` reports its line

### Requirement: Every catalogued language is recognized in every project

codev SHALL recognize the keywords of every language of the catalog in any
main spec or delta, whatever the `language:` of `_codev/config.yaml`. A file
MAY mix keywords of several catalogued languages. The configured language
MUST NOT change whether a file is valid.

#### Scenario: French keywords in an English project

- **GIVEN** a project whose `_codev/config.yaml` holds `language: en`
- **AND** a change whose delta uses `## Exigences AJOUTÉES` and
  `### Exigence :`
- **WHEN** the user runs `codev validate <change>`
- **THEN** the delta is valid

#### Scenario: French keywords in a project with an uncatalogued language

- **GIVEN** a project whose `_codev/config.yaml` holds `language: de`
- **AND** a main spec written with the French keywords
- **WHEN** the user runs `codev validate --specs`
- **THEN** the spec is valid, as it would be with `language: fr`

#### Scenario: Keywords of two languages in one delta

- **GIVEN** a delta with a `## Exigences AJOUTÉES` section holding a
  `### Requirement: Login` with a `#### Scénario : OK`
- **WHEN** the user runs `codev validate <change>`
- **THEN** the delta is valid and carries the requirement `Login` with its
  scenario `OK`

### Requirement: Spelling tolerances of the keywords

codev SHALL match a heading keyword of any catalogued language without
regard to letter case, as it does for English, and SHALL match an accented
letter of a keyword also when it is written without its accent (`Scenario`
for `Scénario`, `AJOUTEES` for `AJOUTÉES`). The colon of a keyword MAY be
preceded by spaces, ordinary or non-breaking, as French typography writes
it. The normative keywords MUST be matched in exact uppercase only.

#### Scenario: A French scenario heading without accent

- **GIVEN** a requirement holding a scenario headed `#### Scenario : Idle`
- **WHEN** the parser reads the file
- **THEN** the requirement carries the scenario `Idle`

#### Scenario: A non-breaking space before the colon

- **GIVEN** a delta whose requirement heading is `### Exigence` followed by
  a non-breaking space, `: Mode sombre`
- **WHEN** the parser reads the delta
- **THEN** the delta carries a requirement named `Mode sombre`, without
  leading space

#### Scenario: A lowercase French normative keyword

- **GIVEN** a requirement whose description is "L'application doit suivre
  le thème du système" and holds no other normative keyword
- **WHEN** the user runs `codev validate <change>`
- **THEN** a finding `requirement_no_shall` reports the requirement

## ADDED Requirements

### Requirement: The merge keeps the language of the main spec

The language of a main spec SHALL be the language, in the `spec-keywords`
catalog, of its `## Requirements` heading. A sync or an archive MUST write
the `### Requirement:` and `#### Scenario:` headings of the blocks it inserts
(`ADDED`) or replaces (`MODIFIED`) with the keywords of the main spec's
language, whatever language the delta is written in. A `RENAMED` operation
MUST replace only the name of the requirement heading and keep its keyword
exactly as written. Descriptions and scenario bodies are copied from the
delta as written: the merge never translates prose or normative keywords.

#### Scenario: English delta merged into a French spec

- **GIVEN** a main spec whose sections are `## Objectif` and `## Exigences`,
  with a requirement `### Exigence : Mode sombre`
- **AND** an `## ADDED Requirements` delta carrying
  `### Requirement: Contraste élevé` with a `#### Scenario: Réglage activé`
- **WHEN** the user runs `codev sync <change>`
- **THEN** the main spec now ends with `### Exigence : Contraste élevé`
  holding `#### Scénario : Réglage activé`
- **AND** the `Mode sombre` block is identical down to the character to
  what it was

#### Scenario: French delta merged into an English spec

- **GIVEN** a main spec written with the English keywords, holding a
  requirement `Login`
- **AND** an `## Exigences MODIFIÉES` delta carrying `### Exigence : Login`
  whose description contains `DOIT`, with a `#### Scénario : OK`
- **WHEN** the user runs `codev sync <change>`
- **THEN** the replaced block is headed `### Requirement: Login` and holds
  `#### Scenario: OK`
- **AND** its description is the delta's, `DOIT` included

#### Scenario: Renaming a requirement of a French spec

- **GIVEN** a main spec holding `### Exigence : Expiration de session`
- **AND** an English `## RENAMED Requirements` delta with
  `FROM: Expiration de session` and `TO: Délai de session`
- **WHEN** the user runs `codev sync <change>`
- **THEN** the heading has become `### Exigence : Délai de session`
- **AND** the description and scenarios of that requirement are identical
  down to the character

#### Scenario: A spec mixing languages follows its Requirements heading

- **GIVEN** a main spec whose sections are `## Purpose` and `## Exigences`
- **AND** an English `ADDED` delta carrying a requirement `Export`
- **WHEN** the user runs `codev sync <change>`
- **THEN** the inserted block is headed `### Exigence : Export`

## MODIFIED Requirements

### Requirement: Creation of a main spec for a new capability

When the delta targets a capability that does not yet have a main spec
under `_codev/specs/`, a sync SHALL create the file `_codev/specs/<path>/spec.md`
from the delta's `## Purpose` and its `ADDED` requirements. The new main
spec MUST be written in the language, in the `spec-keywords` catalog, of the
delta's Purpose heading: its title, its Purpose and Requirements headings,
and the requirement and scenario headings all use that language's keywords.

#### Scenario: New capability created from Purpose and ADDED

- **GIVEN** no main spec under `_codev/specs/user-auth/`
- **AND** a delta carrying `## Purpose` and an `ADDED: Login` requirement
- **WHEN** the user runs `codev sync <change>`
- **THEN** the file `_codev/specs/user-auth/spec.md` now exists
- **AND** it starts with the delta's `## Purpose` section
- **AND** it contains the delta's `Login` requirement under `## Requirements`

#### Scenario: New capability created from a French delta

- **GIVEN** no main spec under `_codev/specs/user-auth/`
- **AND** a delta carrying `## Objectif` and an `## Exigences AJOUTÉES`
  section with `### Exigence : Connexion` and a `#### Scénario : OK`
- **WHEN** the user runs `codev sync <change>`
- **THEN** the file `_codev/specs/user-auth/spec.md` starts with
  `# Spécification User auth`, then `## Objectif` with the delta's text
- **AND** it contains `### Exigence : Connexion` and its
  `#### Scénario : OK` under `## Exigences`

#### Scenario: New capability without Purpose is rejected

- **GIVEN** no main spec under `_codev/specs/x/`
- **AND** a delta carrying only `ADDED` operations without `## Purpose`
- **WHEN** the user runs `codev sync <change>`
- **THEN** no write takes place
- **AND** an error message names the capability, states that `## Purpose` is
  required for a new capability, and recalls the stable code
  `new_capability_without_purpose`

## ADDED Requirements

### Requirement: Structure recognized in every catalogued language

The parser SHALL extract the same structure — Purpose, requirements,
scenarios, delta operations and their payloads — from a file written with the
keywords of any language of the `spec-keywords` catalog as from the same file
written in English, and MUST report the same structural defects, at the same
lines, with the same codes.

#### Scenario: French delta with every operation

- **GIVEN** a delta holding `## Exigences AJOUTÉES` with
  `### Exigence : Mode sombre` and a `#### Scénario : Système sombre`,
  `## Exigences SUPPRIMÉES` with `### Exigence : Thème fixe` followed by
  `**Raison** : <text>` and `**Migration** : <text>`, and
  `## Exigences RENOMMÉES` with the lines `- DE : Ancien nom` and
  `- VERS : Nouveau nom`
- **WHEN** the parser reads the delta
- **THEN** the `ADDED` operation carries `Mode sombre` and its scenario
  `Système sombre`
- **AND** the `REMOVED` operation carries `Thème fixe` with its reason and
  its migration
- **AND** the `RENAMED` operation associates `Ancien nom` with `Nouveau nom`

#### Scenario: French scenario with three hashes

- **GIVEN** a requirement whose scenario is written `### Scénario : Idle`
- **WHEN** the parser reads the file
- **THEN** a structural defect reports the line and indicates that the
  scenario must carry four hashes
- **AND** the requirement still appears in the result, without that scenario

#### Scenario: French delta header in a main spec

- **GIVEN** a main spec file that mistakenly contains an
  `## Exigences AJOUTÉES`
- **WHEN** the parser reads the file
- **THEN** a defect reports the line and specifies that delta headers
  belong only in change files

## MODIFIED Requirements

### Requirement: Localized structural defects

When faced with a malformed file, the parser MUST produce a report naming the
line concerned, the defect type, and a readable message; it SHALL NOT
fail wholesale on a partially recoverable file.

#### Scenario: Scenario written with three hashes

- **GIVEN** a requirement whose scenario is written `### Scenario:` instead of
  `#### Scenario:`
- **WHEN** the parser reads the file
- **THEN** a structural defect reports the line and indicates that the
  scenario must carry four hashes
- **AND** the requirement still appears in the result, without that scenario

#### Scenario: Duplicate requirement within the same section

- **GIVEN** an `## ADDED Requirements` delta containing two requirements with
  exactly the same name
- **WHEN** the parser reads the delta
- **THEN** a defect reports both lines of the duplicate requirements
- **AND** names the `ADDED` section as the location of the conflict

#### Scenario: Delta header in a main spec

- **GIVEN** a main spec file that mistakenly contains an
  `## ADDED Requirements`
- **WHEN** the parser reads the file
- **THEN** a defect reports the line and specifies that delta headers
  belong only in change files

#### Scenario: Unexpected heading inside a delta section

- **GIVEN** an `## ADDED Requirements` section containing a heading
  `### Anforderung: Dunkelmodus` instead of `### Requirement: …`
- **WHEN** the parser reads the delta
- **THEN** an error `delta_unexpected_heading` reports the line
- **AND** its message names the requirement heading of every catalogued
  language, `### Requirement:` and `### Exigence :`
- **AND** the section is also reported as empty with the warning
  `delta_section_empty`

## MODIFIED Requirements

### Requirement: Structural rules beyond the parser

The validator MUST reject as errors the defects that the parser lets
through because they require inspecting the content of a requirement or a
spec: a requirement without a normative keyword in its description, a
requirement with no scenario, a main spec with no extractable requirement.
A normative keyword is one of those of the `spec-keywords` catalog, of any
language — `SHALL`, `MUST`, `DOIT`, `DOIVENT` — in exact uppercase. The
message of a `requirement_no_shall` finding MUST name every accepted
normative keyword.

#### Scenario: Requirement without SHALL or MUST

- **GIVEN** an `## ADDED Requirements` delta with a `### Requirement: X`
  whose descriptive text is "The system does something"
- **WHEN** the validator inspects the file
- **THEN** a finding with code `requirement_no_shall` reports the line of
  the header and names the requirement `X`
- **AND** its message names `SHALL`, `MUST`, `DOIT` and `DOIVENT`

#### Scenario: Requirement with a French normative keyword

- **GIVEN** an `## Exigences AJOUTÉES` delta with a `### Exigence : X`
  whose descriptive text is "L'application DOIT suivre le thème du système"
  and which has a scenario
- **WHEN** the validator inspects the file
- **THEN** no `requirement_no_shall` finding is reported

#### Scenario: Requirement with no scenario at all

- **GIVEN** an `## ADDED Requirements` delta with a `### Requirement: Y`
  followed by its descriptive text but no `#### Scenario:`
- **WHEN** the validator inspects the file
- **THEN** a finding with code `requirement_no_scenario` reports the line
  of the requirement

#### Scenario: Main spec with no requirement

- **GIVEN** a main spec `_codev/specs/x/spec.md` with `## Purpose`
  but whose `## Requirements` is empty
- **WHEN** the validator inspects the spec
- **THEN** a finding with code `spec_no_requirement` reports that the spec
  has no extractable requirement
